content.title: Mitch Johnson Named 2026 NBA All-Star Head Coach | San Antonio Spurs
content.text: Mitch Johnson Named 2026 NBA All-Star Head CoachsasmcaseyFebruary 2, 20265:09 PM CSTSAN ANTONIO (Feb. 1, 2026) – The NBA today announced that San Antonio Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson will represent the Western Conference as a head coach in the 2026 NBA All-Star Game. Johnson becomes the second All-Star head coach in franchise history and the first since Gregg Popovich in 2016.Johnson has led San Antonio to a 33-16 record, third-best mark in the NBA and the Spurs best record through 49 games since the 2016-17 season. Defensively, San Antonio ranks in the top 10 in opponent second-chance points (2nd), fast break points allowed (2nd), opponent field goal percentage (4th) and opponent scoring (7th), while holding the league’s third-best defensive rating (111.4).Under Johnson, San Antonio has the third-most clutch wins in the NBA (17), with a 124.8 offensive rating in clutch situations (3rd). Additionally, from opening night on Oct. 22 through Jan. 11, the Spurs scored 100+ points in 39 consecutive games, the second-longest streak in the NBA this season and have reached the 100-point mark in 46 of 49 games overall.
